questions.evidence:
Class Nine is choosing a theme for its wall display. Eighteen students attend the lunchtime meeting. Ten choose local wildlife, six choose favorite books, and two leave their slips blank. The remaining twelve classmates are away at club activities.

After lunch, Owen writes that most of the class chose wildlife. His friend Yu asks what class means in that sentence. Wildlife received the most votes at the meeting, but only ten of all thirty classmates selected it.

The teacher lets the class finish the vote the next morning. Everyone who missed the meeting receives a slip. The first eighteen students keep their original votes, so nobody gets an extra chance simply by attending twice.

Owen changes the first announcement to say wildlife is leading so far. He waits for the remaining slips before writing the final result. A blank slip and an absent student are both different from a vote against a theme.
questions.explanation: 已投票中野生動物領先，尚有十二人未投。
options: Wildlife leads among votes cast, with twelve classmates still to vote.
All blank slips are votes against wildlife.
Most of all thirty students have voted for wildlife.
questions.prompt: Which description is accurate before the final vote?
